evals.prompt: Review a dashboard surface diff. A plain data panel is styled `.dashboard-panel { background: var(--brand-violet-purple); }` and a summary card is styled `.hero-card { background: #f3e8ff; }` described in the PR as 'tinted for emphasis'. Neither is a feedback surface, an app-shell layout, or an interactive state, and nothing in the task asked for a coloured background.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Targets C1 — decorative/brand fill on a neutral surface with no sanctioned reason or request.
evals.expected_output: C1 (Every surface is white-by-default or a sanctioned exception) FAILs: a neutral data panel is painted brand purple and a card is given a pastel tint 'for emphasis' — neither maps to a sanctioned reason (semantic feedback tint, app-shell colorBgLayout grey, or interactive state fill) and there is no evidence the human requested the colour. Fix: remove the fills so both surfaces inherit white colorBgContainer (or, if the colour was actually requested, cite where in the task and keep it as a brand token). This is a C1-only failure — do not re-flag under C3. C2 and C3 pass. Overall: NEEDS FIX.
assertions: Notes the panel/card have no feedback/state/layout role and no request
Does not double-count the same fill under C3

evals.prompt: Review a landing surface. The page wrapper is `.page { background: linear-gradient(135deg, #6a1ebb, #16c49a); }` and a promo card is `.cta-card { background: radial-gradient(circle, #7f58f0, #d7b8ff); }`. Both gradients paint the full surface fill; neither is the AI border-gradient technique (there is no transparent border with a white padding-box fill).
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Targets C2 — gradient used as a surface background/fill, not the AI border-only exception.
evals.expected_output: C2 (No gradient as a background or fill) FAILs: both surfaces use a gradient as their background fill (a linear-gradient page and a radial-gradient card), and neither is the sole sanctioned exception — the AI affordance, where the gradient sits on the border-box only with a white padding-box fill. Fix: replace the gradient fills with a solid token (white colorBgContainer by default), reserving gradients only for the AI border technique. C1 and C3 pass. Overall: NEEDS FIX.
assertions: Identifies both the linear-gradient and radial-gradient surface fills
Notes the AI border-gradient (white padding-box) is the only exception

evals.prompt: Review an inline result panel that is a legitimate semantic feedback surface (an incorrect-answer banner). It is styled `.answer--incorrect { background: #fff1f0; }` — a raw hex literal, even though it is the correct error-tint colour, instead of the semantic token.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Targets C3 — legitimately non-white feedback surface but value is a raw hex instead of a token.
evals.expected_output: C3 (Non-white colour comes from a token, never a raw hex) FAILs: this surface is legitimately non-white (a sanctioned semantic feedback tint, so C1 passes), but the value is a raw `#fff1f0` hex literal rather than the semantic token. Fix: replace the hex with `var(--aha-colorErrorBg)` so the error tint comes from the token. C1 and C2 pass. Overall: NEEDS FIX.
assertions: Confirms the surface is allowed non-white (C1 passes) so the failure is only C3
